fish.name: Teakettle Guppy
fish.flavor: Whistles a thin, anxious note whenever the water approaches a boil. Locals set their morning routines by it.

fish.name: Cinder Sprat
fish.flavor: Schools of them drift like sparks off a campfire. Catching one feels vaguely like catching a snowflake's angry cousin.

fish.name: Bathwater Chub
fish.flavor: Insists on water that is exactly lukewarm and radiates quiet judgment if it isn't. A creature of tremendous, tepid opinions.

fish.name: Grumble Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Mutters constantly in low, resentful bubbles. Nobody knows what about, but everyone agrees it sounds justified.

fish.name: Matchstick Eel
fish.flavor: Thin as a splinter with a bright red head that never quite ignites. It keeps trying, though. You have to admire that.

fish.name: Sulfur Smelt
fish.flavor: Smells exactly how you'd expect. Tastes better than you'd fear, which the smelt considers a personal betrayal.

fish.name: Mudpot Molly
fish.flavor: Wallows in bubbling mud pots and emerges glazed like pottery. Considered good luck to catch one still warm from the kiln.

fish.name: Parboil Perch
fish.flavor: Arrives at the net gently pre-cooked and deeply unbothered about it. Chefs adore it; philosophers avoid it.

fish.name: Griddle Loach
fish.flavor: Presses itself flat against sun-hot stones and sizzles contentedly. Flip it gently; it likes both sides done evenly.

fish.name: Soot Dace
fish.flavor: Leaves little gray fingerprints on everything it touches. Handle one and you'll be dusting your tackle box for a week.

fish.name: Steamwhisker Cat
fish.flavor: Its whiskers trail wisps of steam as it prowls the warm murk. Purrs when hooked, which is unsettling for everyone involved.

fish.name: Kettle Darter
fish.flavor: Zips between rising bubbles like it's late for something. It is never late for anything. It just likes the drama.

fish.name: Pumice Puffer
fish.flavor: Inflates into a perfect sphere of holes and simply floats away from its problems. Naturalists call it buoyant; poets call it brave.

fish.name: Geyser Gulper
fish.flavor: Rides eruptions forty feet into the air with its mouth wide open, swallowing whatever the sky offers. Optimism as a survival strategy.

fish.name: Candlewick Loach
fish.flavor: A pale taper of a fish with a single glowing barbel that gutters in the steam. Old bathers claim it holds a vigil for something long forgotten.

fish.name: Fumarole Flounder
fish.flavor: Lies over steam vents like a lid on a pot, venting little puffs through its gills at scheduled intervals. The schedule is its own business.

fish.name: Cauldron Carp
fish.flavor: Every witch's soup recipe calls for one, and every witch's soup recipe notes it will climb out of the pot and leave, offended, before serving.

fish.name: Slagback Bream
fish.flavor: Wears a crust of cooled lava like a hand-me-down coat, two sizes too heavy. It clanks faintly when it turns.

fish.name: Hiccup Herring
fish.flavor: Swallowed a bubble of geyser steam as a fry and never quite recovered. Each hiccup releases a tiny, apologetic cloud.

fish.name: Obsidian Knifefish
fish.flavor: Edged like fresh volcanic glass and twice as vain about it. It swims sideways past reflective surfaces on purpose.

fish.name: Witchbath Koi
fish.flavor: Found only in springs where someone once made a sincere wish. Its scales rearrange overnight into patterns nobody remembers choosing.

fish.name: Glassblower's Eel
fish.flavor: Translucent amber and warm to the touch, as if pulled from the furnace mid-shaping. Hold it to the light and you can see tomorrow's weather, slightly wrong.

fish.name: Smokering Ray
fish.flavor: Glides through the shallows exhaling perfect rings of mineral steam. It has never once been asked to perform and never once stopped.

fish.name: Pyroclast Angler
fish.flavor: Dangles a smoldering ember over its jaws in water that should extinguish it, and doesn't. The other fish have decided not to think about it.

fish.name: Simmerwyrm
fish.flavor: A long, patient coil that keeps its pool at a rolling simmer just by being in a good mood. On bad days the water goes still, and bathers politely leave.

fish.name: The Bathhouse Bannik
fish.flavor: A bearded, grandfatherly presence that surfaces only when the springs are empty and the towels are folded. Leave it soap and it will leave you luck; splash it and leave the region.

fish.name: Kettlewitch's Ladle
fish.flavor: Shaped precisely like a long-handled ladle, because it once was one. The kettlewitch stirred her spring too lovingly, and the spring stirred back.

fish.name: Salamander Sovereign
fish.flavor: Wears a crown of cooling crust that cracks and reforms with each slow breath. The fire salamanders of legend bow to something, and it is this.

fish.name: Grandmother Geyser
fish.flavor: The great spring erupts on her breathing, and has for nine hundred years; the town clock is set to her, not the other way around. When she finally takes your line, the whole valley holds its steam.

fish.name: The First Warmth
fish.flavor: Before there were hearths, before there were suns to set, something warm coiled at the bottom of the world's first pool and decided to stay. Every hot spring since is just the memory of where it has rested.
